conceptBreakdown.heading: 4.1 Markovnikov's Rule & Kharasch Peroxide Effect
conceptBreakdown.title: 4.1 Markovnikov's Rule & Kharasch Peroxide Effect

summaryBox.title: A_E Regioselectivity
summaryBox.takeaway: Markovnikov: H⁺ adds to carbon with more H's (forming stable carbocation). Kharasch: HBr + peroxide gives Anti-Markovnikov via Br• radical.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
KHARASCH PEROXIDE MECHANISM (HBr ONLY)

Initiation:   R-O-O-R → 2 RO• ──[+HBr]──► ROH + Br•
Propagation:  R-CH=CH₂ + Br• → R-ĊH-CH₂Br (More stable 2° radical!)
              R-ĊH-CH₂Br + HBr → R-CH₂-CH₂Br (Anti-Markovnikov) + Br•

Why Peroxide Effect Fails for HCl & HI (NEST TRAP):
• HCl: H-Cl bond is too strong (431 kJ/mol); step 1 is endothermic.
• HI: H-I bond is weak, but I• radicals combine to form I₂ (2I• → I₂) instead of adding to alkenes.
conceptBreakdown.content:
• **Markovnikov Addition**: The electrophile $\text{H}^+$ adds to the $sp^2$ carbon with more hydrogen atoms to generate the more stable carbocation intermediate.
• **Anti-Markovnikov Peroxide Effect (Kharasch Effect)**: Applies **STRICTLY to $\text{HBr}$** in the presence of organic peroxides via a free-radical chain mechanism. $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{HI}$ fail this test.

conceptBreakdown.title: 4.2 Alkene Hydration Pathways Comparison Matrix
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ALKENE HYDRATION MATRIX
                                     │
     ┌───────────────────────────────┼───────────────────────────────┐
     ▼                               ▼                               ▼
ACID-CATALYZED HYDRATION        OXYMERCURATION-DEMERCURATION    HYDROBORATION-OXIDATION
(H⁺ / H₂O)                      (OMDM)                          (HBO)
├── Markovnikov addition        ├── Markovnikov addition        ├── Anti-Markovnikov addition
├── Carbocation intermediate    ├── Cyclic mercurinium ion      ├── Syn-addition of H₂O
└── PRONE TO REARRANGEMENTS     └── NO REARRANGEMENTS           └── BH₃·THF → H₂O₂/OH⁻
conceptBreakdown.content:
1. **Acid-Catalyzed Hydration**: $\text{H}^+/\text{H}_2\text{O}$ adds via classical carbocation; prone to 1,2-hydride/methyl shifts (*e.g., 3-methyl-1-butene yields 2-methyl-2-butanol*).
2. **OMDM**: $\text{Hg(OAc)}_2 / \text{H}_2\text{O}$ followed by $\text{NaBH}_4$. Adds $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ Markovnikov **WITHOUT rearrangement** via a cyclic mercurinium ion.
3. **HBO**: $\text{BH}_3\cdot\text{THF}$ followed by alkaline $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$. Adds $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ in an **Anti-Markovnikov, Syn-addition** manner.

quickRevision: Peroxide effect applies ONLY to HBr.
OMDM gives Markovnikov product with NO rearrangements.
